title: Maestro Game IR
description: Engine-agnostic intermediate representation for a Maestro game. The model emits THIS (plain JSON, in-distribution), and a deterministic backend compiles it to an engine (Ren'Py today; RPGMaker / web / Twine later). Visual assets are referenced by id; their generation spec lives in the separate asset manifest (asset_manifest.schema.json), never as file paths here. Design rationale lives in game_ir_decisions.md.

meta.description: Human-facing framing. Premise/title; not load-bearing for the compiler.

characters.description: Character cast. A dialogue line's `speaker` MUST be an id here (or null for narration).

backgrounds.description: Scene backgrounds lifted from the asset manifest. A node's `location` resolves to an `id` here.

items.description: Inventory items. An id used by a take/use action or an item condition MUST be declared here.

flags.description: Boolean puzzle/story flags, default false. Set by effects, read by conditions.

variables.description: Numeric state (e.g. trust, gold, days). Read by `var` conditions, changed by set_var/add_var effects.

start.description: Where play begins. A place (PnC/RPG) and/or a node (VN, or an opening cutscene). At least one required.

spawn.description: RPG: player start cell within the place.

goal.description: OPTIONAL win condition. When satisfiable, a win action / ending becomes legal. Omit entirely for open-ended games with no win state.

places.description: Spatial scenes the player navigates. A 'room' (PnC), a 'town'/'world_map'/'interior' (RPG), or empty (VN). Each holds interactables. Reachability is a graph walk over move/talk targets — no engine parsing.

nodes.description: Dialogue scenes — the genre-invariant core. A list of spoken lines + a terminal control (jump / menu / return / end). Identical across VN, PnC, RPG.

combat_model.description: Projection hint for HOW combat plays. The ONLY place the loop style is named — per-ability data never encodes it. none = no combat. auto = engine's default.

encounters.description: Combat scenes (combatants placed in an arena + win/lose + node_end resolution). A fight is ENTERED by a start_combat action on any interactable; it resolves out via the encounter's on_victory/on_defeat.

progression.description: Combat's projection of the growth loop (present only when combat is): who the player fights as, which LEVELED variable is the XP pool, and what a level-up does to combat stats. XP production is ordinary effects — victories add the loser's xp_yield to xp_var; any other action can feed it too. Player combat stats persist across fights.

player.description: combatant id the player fights as in every encounter and wild fight.

xp_var.description: a LEVELED variable (declares level_var/per_level) that accumulates XP.

growth.description: Combat stat increases applied at each level-up (level-up also heals depletables to their grown max).

sprite.description: Optional asset id for the neutral portrait/sprite (the base expression).

expressions.description: Optional per-emotion sprite variants ({emotion: image_file}). A line's `emotion` selects one; falls back to `sprite` (neutral) when absent. Derived by the asset pipeline, not hand-authored.

sex.description: Optional; drives sprite and spoken-voice casting (a TTS bank is filtered by it before the deterministic pick).

tts_voice.description: Optional explicit TTS speaker preset; overrides the sex-filtered pick.

examine.description: Flavor text when inspected in inventory.

min.description: Optional clamp floor (advisory — enforced by the compiler if at all).

level_var.description: Makes this a LEVELED variable: the runtime keeps the named variable (also declared in `variables`) derived as floor(value / per_level) + 1. Any effect that feeds this variable (a harvest outcome, a victory yield, a choice) advances the level; any condition can gate on the level variable. Requires per_level.

per_level.description: Points per level for a leveled variable. Requires level_var.

kind.description: room = PnC scene (click hotspots); world_map/town/interior = RPG (a walkable tile grid). The runtime picks the presenter from this — room => point-and-click, the rest => the WASD overworld. The compiler picks the engine projection from it too.

background.description: Asset id for a PnC room's backdrop. Walkable maps render their tiles and need no background.

tiles.description: RPG map painted as a char grid. Required for world_map/town/interior; ignored for room. Grid size = the shape of `rows`. Each char resolves via `legend` (or the built-in defaults) to a role: open (walkable) or blocked (wall). interactable/spawn cells must be open tiles within [0,width) x [0,height).

rows.description: One string per grid row (top to bottom); each char is a tile. All rows same length.

legend.description: Maps a single tile char -> its role + theme. Built-in defaults ('.'ground ','path '#'wall 'T'tree '~'water '%'rock) need no entry; declare only new chars or overrides.

role.description: open = walkable, blocked = wall/obstacle. The only tile property the engine reads.

theme.description: Free cosmetic label (drives the tile's look), e.g. 'frozen stream', 'neon barrier'.

interactables.description: Everything the player can click (PnC) or step on / talk to (RPG). At least one must lead elsewhere or the place is a dead end.

layout.description: The authored map PLAN for a walkable place (features on a coarse region grid). maestro.map_builder rasterizes it into `tiles` at write time; engines read only `tiles`. Kept for re-authoring/edits.

anchors.description: feature/exit id -> {x, y} open cell in front of it, emitted by the map builder. Used to resolve interactable positions and cross-zone move spawns; engines ignore it.

footprints.description: feature id -> {x, y, w, h, kind, label} cell rect the map builder stamped for a solid feature. The overworld presenter draws a generated object sprite (feature_<slug>.png) over the rect when the asset exists.

encounter_table.description: Wild fights for a walkable zone: each step onto an open tile rolls `rate`; on a hit the player fights one combatant drawn from `entries` by weight, its stats scaled by `tier`. Defeat in a wild fight respawns at the zone spawn (no game over) — authored encounters keep their on_defeat stakes.

tier.description: Stat multiplier for this zone's variant of the combatant.

label.description: Player-facing name of the thing (hotspot tooltip / NPC name).

sprite.description: Optional asset id (an NPC/object drawn on the map).

position.description: Where an interactable sits. Exactly ONE projection: `rect` (on-screen pixel box — PnC/VN, 1280x720 canvas) or `cell` (grid tile — RPG). Room for more projections later.

action.description: What happens on interact. The CLOSED verb vocabulary — exactly the six shapes the prompts already enumerate. Discriminated by `type`.

text.description: Description shown, then return to the place.

node.description: node id to play, then return to the place.

spawn.description: Arrival in the target walkable place: a resolved tile {cell:{x,y}}, or the transitional layout form {feature: '<feature/exit id in the target zone>'} which write_place resolves to a cell as soon as the target zone exists.

action_use.description: The interact verb: ordered `clauses` evaluated top-down — the first whose `requires` holds fires its outcome; if none match, `fallback` fires. A simple lock is one clause + a fallback. An UNCONDITIONAL effect (e.g. 'pray → set a flag, always') is just a `fallback` with no clauses. Must carry at least one of `clauses`/`fallback`.

clauses.description: Evaluated in order; first match wins. Each requires a REAL condition (never an empty {}). Omit entirely for an unconditional outcome — put it in `fallback`.

fallback.description: Outcome when no clause matches — or, with no clauses, the UNCONDITIONAL outcome (always fires).

requires.description: Defaults to the top-level goal if omitted.

action_start_combat.description: Enter a combat encounter. Any interactable can start a fight (an aggressive NPC, a trapped chest, a boss door); resolution flows out via the encounter's on_victory/on_defeat.

requires.description: Optional gate (only ambushes if a flag is set, etc.).

outcome.description: The result of a use/choice: say something and/or change state.

condition.description: A boolean over game state. Leaf (item / flag / var comparison) or composite (all / any / not).

oneOf.description: Numeric comparison. `value` is a literal number OR another variable, e.g. {var:'sleight_of_hand', op:'>', value:{var:'perception'}}.

operand.description: A number, or a reference to another variable's value.

oneOf.description: Set a variable to an absolute value.

location.description: VN: background asset id (resolves to `backgrounds`) shown for this scene. Omitted by PnC dialogue nodes called from a place.

lines.description: Ordered dialogue beats. Effects attach to a specific line so timing is explicit.

speaker.description: character id, or null for narration.

emotion.description: Optional facial expression for the speaker on this line (default neutral). Selects the speaker's matching sprite variant; ignored for narration (speaker null).

effects.description: Optional state changes applied AFTER this line is spoken (give item, set flag, change var).

node_end.description: Terminal control after the lines. jump = continue to another node; menu = branch on player choice; return = back to the calling place (PnC talk / open-world loop); end = the story ends here (a definitive ending).

target.description: node id this choice jumps to.

requires.description: Optional: choice only shown/enabled when met.

stat.description: A declared combat/character stat. The game defines its own stat system rather than the schema hardcoding hp/mp/etc. `role` tells the engine projection HOW to use the stat without encoding a combat loop.

min.description: Floor. For resource_depletable, reaching min typically means defeated (engine projection decides).

max.description: Ceiling. Clamp semantics committed: the compiler MUST clamp to [min,max] on every stat mutation.

role.description: resource_depletable = HP-like, depletes, hitting min = out of fight. resource_regenerating = MP/stamina-like, spent and recovered. modifier = feeds formulas (attack/defense). rating = static descriptor (level/tier), rarely mutated.

faction.description: Whose side a combatant is on. Targeting and victory/defeat conditions resolve against this. Engine-independent.

combatant.description: What an entity IS in combat: its stat block, abilities, and tie back to a character for name/sprite. Pure data — survives unchanged from text to 2D to 3D.

character.description: Optional character id for display name/sprite. Combat identity is separate from narrative identity.

stats.description: This combatant's values for declared stats. A stat id not listed uses the stat's declared default.

abilities.description: ability ids this combatant can use.

xp_yield.description: XP awarded to the player for defeating this combatant.

ability.description: What an action DOES, never how it looks or how time passes. Cost + targeting intent + stat effects + optional gate. The engine projection owns animation, frame data, hitboxes.

cost.description: Resource cost to use. Empty/absent = free.

stat.description: stat id, should be a resource_* role.

effects.description: What happens to each target. Reuses combat_effect (stat-aware) — distinct from the narrative `effect` def which mutates game flags/vars/items.

requires.description: Optional gate (learned the spell, has the weapon). Reuses your existing condition def.

targeting.description: WHO/WHERE an ability hits, as engine-independent intent. shape + faction + range describe geometry abstractly; the projection turns `cone` into a turn-based group-hit, a 3D collider, or 'the front rank' in text.

shape.description: Abstract hit shape. self = caster. single = one target. all = every valid-faction combatant. line/cone/area = spatial spreads the projection realizes per dimension.

faction.description: Which side is a legal target relative to the user.

range.description: Engagement distance intent. melee = adjacent/close, ranged = at distance. The projection decides what that means spatially.

combat_effect.description: A change an ability makes to a target's stat, or a status/narrative effect. Kept separate from the top-level `effect` def: that one mutates world state (flags/vars/items), this one operates on combatant stats and statuses. They share spirit, not shape.

oneOf.description: Modify a stat. `op` + formula. damage/heal are sugar over a signed delta the projection applies and clamps.

stat.description: stat id affected on the target.

op.description: damage = reduce (mitigated by modifiers per formula), heal = restore, set = absolute, add = signed delta unmitigated.

oneOf.description: Apply or remove a status (poison, stun, shield). Statuses are declared like flags but live on a combatant.

duration.description: Engine-interpreted: turns (turn-based) or seconds (real-time). Units are a projection concern; the number is intent.

oneOf.description: Bridge back to world state — let a combat outcome set a story flag/var (e.g. 'spared_the_boss'). Reuses your narrative effect def verbatim.

formula.description: How a magnitude is computed, as data. base + optional stat scaling. Deliberately minimal — the projection evaluates it; it does NOT encode RNG/crit/turn logic. Absent = the engine's default for that op.

scales_with.description: stat id on the USER whose value scales the effect.

status.description: A declared transient condition a combatant can carry (poison/stun/shield). Per-tick or gating behavior is the projection's to interpret from the effects + role.

tick.description: Optional per-interval effects (poison damage). Interval is a projection concern.

blocks_action.description: true = afflicted combatant cannot act (stun). Engine honors per its loop.

encounter.description: Combat as a spatial scene. A place subtype: combatants positioned in it, win/lose conditions, and node_end transitions on resolution. The combat LOOP (turn order / real-time) is NOT here — it's a projection choice driven by top-level combat_model.

background.description: Asset id for the arena backdrop/map.

combatants.description: Who's in the fight and where they stand. position reuses your existing projection oneOf (rect/cell, + transform when 3D lands).

defeat.description: Defaults to 'all player-faction defeated' if omitted.

on_victory.description: Where play flows on win. Reuses node_end — combat resolves back into dialogue/navigation like everything else.

on_defeat.description: Where play flows on loss (often end:game_over, or a jump to a setback node).

encounter_condition.description: How a fight ends. Faction wipe is the common case; flag/var lets you express survive-N, escape, protect-the-NPC via the existing condition system.

oneOf.description: Win/lose on an arbitrary game-state condition (e.g. var:turns_survived >= 5, flag:reached_exit). Reuses your condition def.

action.text: A key, tucked under a rag.

lines.speaker: warden
lines.text: You won't find the key. I made sure of that.
His eyes flick to the drawer, just once.

lines.speaker: elias
lines.text: I saw your dad at the funeral. He looked... relieved.

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: My mother wasn't a good person. It still feels wrong to see it.
A loud bang sounds from downstairs.

choices.text: Palm the letter while she's distracted

lines.text: The letter is in your pocket before she turns.
The door clicks shut behind you.
